newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
- A Federal advisory panel suggested the nation consider investing part of its Social Security revenues in the stock market to insure the solvency of the retirement programme.

- The idea of investing Social Security revenues in the stock market brings up many concerns, including the question of whether a President or Federal Reserve head would have a conflict in making policy decisions that could send the markets into the tank, imperilling the returns on funds in which every American family would have a stake.
- The New York City Council Speaker said he would form a commission to propose revisions to the City Charter with the goal of shifting the balance of power in city government away from the mayor.

- Newt Gingrich battled for his political future, taking three hours in a closed meeting to explain his ethics violations to the Republicans he is counting on to re-elect him as House Speaker on Tuesday.
- President Clinton appealed to the nation's clergy to help him create "a sense of reconciliation, the right sort of spirit" for the nation to grapple with its social problems.

- The Supreme Court ruled that Federal judges imposing sentences on convicted defendants may -- and in certain circumstances must -- take into account not only the crimes of which the defendants were convicted but also additional charges of which juries found them not guilty.

- Theologians took note when the Vatican's doctrinal authorities found a 72-year-old Sri Lankan priest guilty of having "deviated from the integrity of the truth of the Catholic faith" and, in a rare move, formally cast him out of the communion of the church last week.
